title: Sinusoids: peak, RMS, frequency and phase of the mains supply
examples: Why is 230 V mains 325 V peak?
How do I find the period of a 50 Hz wave?

curves.label: Mains voltage
curves.ask: What is the peak voltage of the mains?

explain.say: Plug a phone charger into a wall in Delhi and it receives a voltage that swings smoothly up and down 50 times every second. That shape is a sinusoid, a sine wave. The curve on the board is the real Indian mains. Let's read four numbers off it: the peak, the RMS value, the frequency and the phase.

draw.text: Sinusoids: peak, RMS, frequency and phase of the mains supply

curves.label: Mains voltage
curves.ask: What is the peak voltage of the mains?

explain.say: Look at the top of the wave. The peak, or amplitude, is about 325 volts, the most the voltage ever reaches. Half a cycle later it hits minus 325 volts, pushing the other way. So why does everyone call it 230 volts? Any guess?

curves.label: Mains voltage
curves.ask: What is the peak voltage of the mains?

explain.say: Because 230 volts is the RMS value, short for root mean square. It is the steady DC voltage that would heat a resistor just as much. For a sine wave, RMS is the peak divided by the square root of 2: 325 over 1.414 is 230 volts. See the flat line? Is the RMS value bigger or smaller than the peak?

curves.label: Mains voltage
curves.ask: What is the peak voltage of the mains?

explain.say: Smaller, about 71 percent of it. Now time. One full cycle takes 20 milliseconds, called the period, T. Frequency is cycles per second, one over T, so 1 over 0.02 seconds is 50 hertz. Engineers also use angular frequency, omega, equal to 2 pi f, about 314 radians per second. What would the period be at 60 hertz, as in the USA?

curves.label: Mains voltage
curves.ask: What is the peak voltage of the mains?

explain.say: About 16.7 milliseconds. Finally, phase. The new wave on the board has the same size and frequency but peaks later, by 60 degrees, a sixth of a cycle. We say it lags by 60 degrees. Wonderful! Exam tip: AC meters show RMS unless they say otherwise. Challenge: the US supply is 120 volts RMS. What is its peak?

curves.ask: What is the peak voltage of the mains?

faq.q: What is the peak voltage of the mains?
faq.a: For a 230 volt RMS supply the peak is 230 times the square root of 2, about 325 volts. The voltage swings between plus and minus 325 volts every cycle.
asks: Why is 230 V mains actually 325 V peak?

faq.a: RMS stands for root mean square. It is the DC value that would deliver the same heating power to a resistor. For a pure sine wave it equals the peak divided by the square root of 2.

faq.q: What is the period of a sine wave?
faq.a: The period is the time for one complete cycle. It is one over the frequency, so 50 hertz gives 20 milliseconds.
asks: How do you find period from frequency?

faq.a: Phase difference is how far one wave is shifted in time relative to another, measured in degrees of a 360 degree cycle. A wave that peaks later is said to lag.
asks: What does lagging by 60 degrees mean?

faq.a: Angular frequency, omega, is 2 pi times the frequency, measured in radians per second. For 50 hertz it is about 314 radians per second.

facts: India, the UK and most of Europe use 230 volts at 50 hertz, while the USA uses 120 volts at 60 hertz.
Japan uses 50 hertz in the east of the country and 60 hertz in the west.

quiz.say: A sine wave has a peak of 170 volts. What is its RMS value?
quiz.show: A sine wave has a peak of 170 V. What is its RMS value?
quiz.why: RMS is the peak over root 2: 170 divided by 1.414 is about 120 volts.

wrong.1: That multiplies by root 2 instead of dividing.
wrong.2: That halves the peak; RMS divides by 1.414, not 2.

quiz.say: A supply runs at 60 hertz. What is its period?
quiz.show: A supply runs at 60 Hz. What is its period?
quiz.why: T is 1 over f: 1 over 60 is about 0.0167 seconds, which is 16.7 milliseconds.

wrong.1: The period is one over the frequency, not the frequency itself.
wrong.2: That is too short; 6 milliseconds would be about 167 hertz.
